$schema: one unprotected home for the units-at-boot pins. Keys are game names; values are the EXACT `ran` count a Null_ build reports.
$why: These numbers used to be duplicated across .github/workflows/zm-tests.yml, zagent.project.json and run_unit_gate.ps1's -Baseline default. Two of those three are protectedPaths, so bumping a pin was work the agent loop could never do: adding a single test redded a REQUIRED check with zero failing tests, and the fix required editing files `zagent guard` refuses. That made every test-adding ticket unreachable, which is most feature work in a repo whose conventions ask for a test with all new code.
$rule: The gate asserts `ran == baseline` EXACTLY, so a GROWN suite fails with zero failures. Bump the number HERE and nowhere else -- the workflows and zagent.project.json now name the GAME, not the count.
$never: Do NOT pin from a Vulkan_ exe. The same tree reports higher on Vulkan than on Null (a standing +37 gap was measured for Zenithmon), because Vulkan builds also compile the Vulkan-only backend tests. Every consumer of this file runs a Null_ executable.
$coverage: NOT every row here is checked by CI. engine-gate.yml gates Combat and zm-tests.yml gates Zenithmon; NOTHING passes -Game RenderTest, so that row is verified only when somebody runs it locally. A pin nothing reads can drift silently, which is the failure this file exists to prevent -- so treat the RenderTest row as advisory until a workflow gates it, and re-observe it rather than trusting it. Filed as a ticket; do not quietly delete the row, because local cross-game sweeps use it and an engine change genuinely moves it.

baselines.$Zenithmon: ZM boot units. Also narrated in Games/Zenithmon/Docs/Status.md, which stays the human-facing authority for WHY it moved; this file is what the gate reads.
baselines.$Combat: The engine boot pin. A backend-neutral ENGINE unit moves this AND every other game's number in the same commit, because they all boot the same engine suite.
baselines.$RenderTest: Every number in this file is OBSERVED from a real Null_ run, never arithmetic on the previous one -- a computed pin is how a suite that also LOST a test still ratchets green. Do NOT narrate individual bumps here: that note drifts at the next bump (it already did once). git log carries the derivation.
